correctness.rationale: From the two survival functions derive high-frailty survivor weight p(u)=1/(1+exp u) with u=k(exp(ct)-1). Population hazard H=Delta(1+u/k)(A+p), A=a/Delta, has derivative sign g(u)=A+p-(u+k)p(1-p). Its derivative is p(1-p)[(u+k)tanh(u/2)-2], whose bracket strictly increases from -2 to infinity, giving exactly one strict global minimum. At that minimum g=A-1/(exp(u*)-1), vanishing only at u*=log(b/a) and k=kc; g(0)=(k0-k)/4 and g(infty)=A>0. These signs force all four cases, with endpoint zero correctly excluded at k=k0. Nondegenerate Taylor coefficients g_k=-p(1-p), g_uu=p(1-p)(2A+1) give square-root split. Independent root counts at A=1/4 for k=0.1,1.8,2,2.95,3,3.3 matched cases; witness k=2 roots 0.634307250 and 2.418458919.
